Costique River: The defending national champions won their third title, after 1980 and 2043, going 15-2 and beating Eona, Pistolheart, Skeenerland State and Tengus State 34-28 in the final at Kirkwood. Defensive coordinator Pascal Northbury left to become Ranroman's head coach and lineman Frode Althardt went first overall in the draft, but tailback Antonella Cisneros, cornerback Deja Maygate and safety Ernest Steinmeier return and five-star lineman Lourdes Buenalarga arrives. Voters gave them 57 of the 60 first-place ballots, and the repeat bid opens at home against UHMM.
Tengus State: A 16-1 season, nine conference wins and a place in the final ended with a 34-28 loss to Costique River, and the school's only title is still 2026. Quarterback Beatrice Peatbourne, the Ryskamp winner, went in the first round, but Layla Smith is in year 18, Abena Upshaw has arrived from Pistolheart as defensive coordinator, and five-star quarterback Dahye Lurong is the new face. Defensive coordinator Rhys Fontenot left to run Cherry Lake, and the schedule opens at home against Grizzly Hills.
North Hatesei: Twenty-one national titles, more than any other team in the preseason top 25, and a 10-4 season that ended with a 20-17 round-two loss to Marblehead after a first-round bye. Offensive lineman Katarina Kleinhuber and cornerback Kirovei Eisemyr went in the first round, with lineman Rowena Rowridge, safety Adebayo Mensah and cornerback Harendra Gangakumar still on the roster and five-star receiver Sidney Langwell arriving. Perla Notaro is in year four with her whole staff intact, the opener is at Crayellan, and the season ends at Hatesei.
Eona: Three titles, the last in 2042, and a 10-4 year that ended in round two against Costique River after a 41-7 win over Ediville State. Tyrell Kingsmond and Tavesei Roresei went in the first round, but cornerback Varun Chalhoub and tailbacks Verity Peatham and Fiona Peatshaw return, with five-star offensive lineman Torben Tannenbrunner joining them. Hollis Upshaw is in year eight, the opener is at home against Spirit of Light, and the season closes at home against Central Stanton.
Rogaela State: A 14-1 season with a perfect 9-0 in the conference, a round-two win over Yrei Trobniy and a quarterfinal loss to Marblehead at the Lumber Bowl. The staff under Rami Campbell, in year 19, is untouched and only two players were drafted, both in the fifth round; quarterback Spiros Kyriapoulos, lineman Konrad Kalthauer and tight end Louniya Tetreimyr return and five-star receiver Vladislav Dememelis arrives. The opener is at home against Krobe State and the season closes at home against Dietsche.
Central Stanton: Eight titles and a 10-5 year that included wins over Marines and Keeper before a quarterfinal loss to Tengus State at the Redwood Bowl. Linebacker Kanei Lorresei went in the first round, but William Brookborough is in year two, tailback Nemiy Tomselniy and lineman Rongrong Fujiguchi are back, and five-star cornerback Eleanor Zlatarek arrives. The schedule opens at home against Coachville College and ends at Eona.
Skeenerland State: A 12-4 year with first-round and round-two wins, a quarterfinal win over UNN at the Star Bowl and a 31-27 semifinal loss to Costique River; the school has no title. Both coordinators left to become head coaches, Ravi Kamau at Eona State and Aliyah Radovsky at Ranroman State, and Ji-woo Hall, in year 16, replaced them with Nia Berg and Hwanki Ji, who came from Ranroman State. Lineman Bassam Somakanth and George Laville went in the first round, and five-star lineman Clemence Marshford arrives.
Pistolheart: A 10-4 season ended in the quarterfinal against Costique River at the 501 Bowl after a round-two win over Eastern State, and they are still without a title. Defensive coordinator Abena Upshaw left for Tengus State and Antoine Anysei came from Marblehead to run the offense. Tage Ludendorf is in year six, safety Lourdes Terralarga, lineman Viola Theokopoulos and cornerback Kysei Woolhurst return, and the opener is at home against Coastal Ranroman.
UNN: A 12-3 season, three titles and a quarterfinal loss to Skeenerland State at the Star Bowl after a round-two win over South Antiragal. Linebacker Zbigniew Chidambaram and receiver Evangelos Lambrmatos went in the first round, offensive coordinator Waimarie Spottedhorse left to coach Roosevelt State, and Esperanza Caraobruno is in year eight. Quarterbacks Raviy Messei and Tevin Langwood are both back, five-star receiver Youngchul Gwang-Ung arrives, and the opener is at home against UN Steelbridge.
Roosevelt: The 2044 champions went 9-4, and a first-round loss to Yrei Trobniy, 19-7, ended the run of the defending title. Cornerback Yansa Ironotter and safety Mathis Lefort went in the second round, but Tane Fifita is in year five with the whole staff back, quarterback Gaspard Schneebruck, receiver Hala Wenli and lineman Paytah El-Tahir return, and five-star tailback Andres Cabrabosque arrives. The opener is at home against Kaji Kita State and the season closes at Roosevelt State.
Eastern State: One title, 2040, and a 10-4 year that included a first-round win over Palisades and a round-two loss to Pistolheart, 17-9. Quarterback Heriberto Holmhus went in the first round, but Bhaskar El-Mahdi is in year six with the staff intact, and tailback Lamont Nwasowah, cornerback Chiyo Xiangpei and lineman Katya Ulutalo return with five-star linebacker Andres Vegaflores arriving. The opener is at home against Western Antiragal and the finale is at home against Keeper.
Marblehead: The run to the semifinals began with a win over Lito Rock State, then North Hatesei in round two and Rogaela State at the Lumber Bowl before a 38-7 loss to Tengus State at the Copper Bowl, a 12-5 year. Lineman Danica Vlahos went second overall and safety Maoxin Taoduo in the first round, and offensive coordinator Antoine Anysei left for Pistolheart. Onawa Khan is in year 17, linebacker Devonte Durmore and tight end Nils Weinbrandt return, five-star receiver Esi Amanse arrives, and the opener is at East Costique.
Barhold: Five titles, the latest in 2023, and an 8-4 year that stopped short of the playoff. Lineman Ghislaine Vignascio went in the first round, but Darnell Ellery is in year seven with his whole staff in place, tight end Sorei Peylemyr, lineman Arjun Oluchukwu and receivers Francesca Passettoni and Giovanni Torrini return, and the schedule opens at home against Gordon-Shipp. The finale is at Barhold State.
Kaji Daun: Four titles, the last in 2032, and a 7-5 year with 5-4 in the conference, outside the playoff. Henrik Moreau is in year six, Axel Osterberg arrives from Crayellan as offensive coordinator, and cornerback Waimarie Crookedcreek, lineman Kyungja Un-Ho and quarterback Louniya Dahlvik return. The opener is at Keytommiyr and the season ends at home against Kaji Kita.
Ciarralotta Tech: A 10-4 year with 8-1 in the conference, a first-round bye and a round-two loss to Skeenerland State, 45-28; the school has no title. Lineman Palmira Fiorerini went in the first round and Rania El-Aziz in the second, but Uili Tendulkar is in year eight with the staff intact, lineman Terrell Kofkah, receiver Aurelio Midse and tailback Litowa Mesyosei return, and five-star receiver Zhihao Lundlund arrives. The opener is at home against Westburg and the finale is at home against Ciarralotta State.
Yrei Trobniy: A 10-5 season included a first-round win over Roosevelt and a round-two loss to Rogaela State, and the school's one title is 1951. Linebacker Rashad Vinter went in the first round, Hollis Heathcote is in year eight, and cornerback Guowei Zafeikos, lineman Vasudev Schneewetter, tight end Uchenna Northson and quarterback Rongrong Ju-Hwan are back, with five-star safety Katya Stanidis arriving. The opener is at home against Ranroman.
Ranroman State: Four titles, the last in 2037, and a 4-8 year with 2-7 in the conference, the worst record of any team in the preseason top 25. Aliyah Radovsky is the new head coach, hired from Skeenerland State, where she was the defensive coordinator, and both coordinators are in their first year. Quarterback Dulce Navamayor, safety Istas Ironcloud, tailback Romain Nordmark and cornerback Omyr Deyveiro return, and the opener is at home against Lornaman.
Crayellan: Six titles, the last in 2011, and an 8-5 year with 6-3 in the conference. Loredana Neraavanti went in the first round, offensive coordinator Axel Osterberg left for Kaji Daun, and Oksana Stanakis is in year three. Lineman Tavesei Eitravaw, receiver Selvaw Grünbrandt, lineman Huiling Stendahl and safety Vincenza Saintlac return, and the opener is at home against North Hatesei.
Park Island: An 8-4 season with 5-4 in the conference and the Freshman of the Year, quarterback Consuelo Neulac. Two first-round picks, lineman Dieter Eisenhuber and receiver Jagdish El-Sahli, are gone, and both coordinators left to become head coaches, Poppy Hollerbach at Barhold Valley and Hosei Joroviy at Costique, so Holaniy Tirreniy and Prudence Northton are in their first year. Florian Saintfour is in year three, linebacker Rocio Bonichelli and lineman Umeko Yukitani are back, and the opener is at home against Diveo State.
Will Tech: Ten titles, the last in 2002, and a 9-4 year that ended in a 27-22 first-round loss to New Madrid. Linebacker Enapay Manuanua went in the second round, but Wilhelmina Kleinmann is in year eight with the whole staff, safety Haneya Elmwick, tight end Dandan Cheon-Gil, quarterback Rosalie Verregard and kicker Sami Kalyanswamy return, and the opener is at Costique. The season closes at Dove Island.
Keeper: A 10-4 season with a first-round bye ended in a 27-24 round-two loss at home to Central Stanton, and the school has no title. Linebacker Sami Yawmah went in the first round, Xavier Lindqvist is in year six with the staff intact, and tight end Dev Raghunathan, receivers Wanda Apodakis and Savitri Al-Samarrai and tailback Wanda Chikelu return. The opener is at home against Ciarralotta and the finale is at Eastern State.
Ciarralotta State: An 8-4 year with 6-3 in the conference, outside the playoff, and the school has no title. Tyrell Marshden is in year two, linebacker Arjun Baili, lineman Peymyr Ainovaw and receiver Zhihao Go-Su return, and four-star quarterback Oksana Ramarajan is in the class. The schedule opens at Orlot and ends at Ciarralotta Tech.
UFNH: An 8-4 year, no title yet, and two first-round picks, lineman Sixten Schneehardt and tight end Akosua Gyesowah. Moritz Lamehawk is in year six, lineman Katsuo Tanitani, cornerback Belen Herrdura, safety Nadia Thornbourne and punter Cortez Brookwell return, and the opener is at home against Ekralund State. The finale is at Fiota Bay.
Dietsche: Two titles, 2005 and 2019, and a 7-5 year with 5-4 in the conference. Sora Yamamoto is in year eight, tight end Valdemar Lindqvist is gone, and linebackers Uchenna Zamorano and Riku Madhumoorthy and linemen Anei Hanlaniy and Estevaw Teyresei lead the returnees. The opener is at home against Greene and the season ends at Rogaela State.
Hatesei: Four titles, the last in 1986, and an 8-4 year with 6-3 in the conference. Offensive coordinator Kadhim Nagarajan left to coach Dove Island, Freya Dahlqvist is in year five, and safety Bogdana Radzinsky, tight end Sybil Herrreal and linebacker Riku Birkeborg return. The opener is at home against Wolford and the finale is at home against North Hatesei.
